trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR (reported, not fixed). (1) VERIFIED CORRECT - the branching identity Res^{H_k}_{H_3} rho_lambda = (+)_mu f^{lambda/mu} rho_mu is standard, and the substitution reproduces the statement's a_lambda/b_lambda split exactly. Self-consistency check at lambda = [2,1]: f^{[2,1]/[3]} = f^{[2,1]/[1^3]} = 0, f^{[2,1]/[2,1]} = 1, giving chi = -1 - h^2, matching Table 1. (2) VERIFIED CORRECT - 'f^{lambda/[2,1]} = 0 iff lambda is a single row [k] or a single column [1^k]' is right: lambda contains [2,1] iff it has at least 2 rows and 2 columns. (3) VERIFIED CORRECT - every f^{lambda/[2,1]} in Table 2 recomputed by counting linear extensions of the skew shape: [2,1] -> 1; [3,1] -> 1 (one cell); [2,2] -> 1 (one cell); [3,1,1] -> 2; [3,2] -> 2; [3,2,1] -> 6 (three incomparable cells, 3!); [4,2,1] -> 12 (four cells with one same-row order constraint, 4!/2). Conjugates also check: [3,2]' = [2,2,1] and [3,2,1]' = [3,2,1], and dim [3,2,1] = 16 is indeed the largest S_6 irrep. (4) MISLABEL in Table 2: row [2,2] is tagged 'Hook (self-conjugate baryon)'. [2,2] is self-conjugate but is NOT a hook - hooks are [k-r,1^r], and the proof's own item 4 defines them that way. (5) THE BRAID WORD PROBLEM recorded on the statement sibling prop:figure-eight-branching-rule applies to every character in this proof.
